title: The Fantasy Arsenal local walk-forward stat model backtest

methodology.walk_forward: Every forecast is frozen at Wednesday 12:00 UTC. Current-season results enter only after the entire source week is final and a conservative 48-hour publication delay has elapsed; target-week and future results are excluded.
methodology.population: Accuracy is active-game conditional. A player-game is included only when saved raw usage indicates the player participated and at least the configured number of earlier games exists.
methodology.safe_expected: A recency-weighted player baseline is sample-shrunk toward the position median, then adjusted using pre-week defense-vs-position evidence and sample-regressed personal opponent history.
methodology.risky: The frozen Safe / Expected schedule path is centered and amplified using player volatility, matchup differences, and home/away context, then normalized back to the same remaining-season expectation.
methodology.defense_predictors: Each defensive statistic is calculated per team-game using only pre-week raw stats. Correlations compare the frozen defensive index with the player's actual result relative to their frozen baseline.
methodology.weather: Historical kickoff weather was not saved in the local archive and is therefore excluded instead of reconstructed or invented.
limitations: Historical season-level team identity can misattribute pre-trade games for players who changed teams during a season.
The test evaluates current model mechanics using rolling historical baselines; equivalent archived preseason projection-source boards do not exist for every tested season.
Active-game conditional accuracy does not measure the separate problem of predicting inactive players or surprise workload changes.

evidence_summary: Safe / Expected lowered MAE by 0.050 points (1.1%) versus Risky.
The best tested defensive strength was 0.35; its MAE advantage over 0.35 was 0.000 points.
The strongest single defensive input was QB fantasy_points_allowed, with absolute rank correlation 0.0642.
Boom recall was 1.9% and bust recall was 2.1%; the current labels are selective but miss most extreme outcomes.

trained_adjustments.source: The Fantasy Arsenal local walk-forward trainer
trained_adjustments.target: weekly PPR points relative to a leakage-safe rolling player baseline

validation.method: Strict rolling-origin feature construction; tune architecture before the 2025 historical benchmark, refit both incumbent and challenger on identical pre-2025 rows, then require at least four newly frozen future weeks before any release recommendation.

promotion.rule: Historical candidate gate: lower 2025 MAE than incumbent by at least 0.01, improve 2025 RMSE by at least 0.001, and lower MAE than the neutral baseline. This reused historical period is not a release holdout; publication additionally requires four frozen future weeks and owner review.
